s9-000-4215f49835241eb7.wav.text: The last piece, and it settles the quiet failure from episode one.

s9-001-830bb608c004ccc1.wav.text: Taking the logarithm of a softmax is the wrong way to compute log softmax, because any probability that underflowed to zero becomes minus infinity.

s9-002-831c9a2b40fa4e58.wav.text: Subtract the log sum exp instead.

s9-003-0dbbcd0161d54aaa.wav.text: Log softmax of x equals x minus log sum exp of x.

s9-004-a4558f6ecee1a203.wav.text: At the vector zero and minus eight hundred, that returns exactly minus eight hundred, where the naive route returns minus infinity.

s9-005-37c5a3603992d2a0.wav.text: Then cross entropy is log sum exp of x, minus the logit at the target index.

s9-006-7d178d73f8d1cea9.wav.text: Notice there is no exponential of the target term anywhere in that.

s9-008-cc105d2729bbac47.wav.text: The gradient of that fused loss is softmax of x, minus the one hot vector of the target.

s9-009-8a91251681377552.wav.text: That is the entire backward pass.

s9-010-e1db51933afe9e9f.wav.text: The logarithm and the exponential cancel so completely that the fused loss is easier to differentiate than either half of it separately, which is why every framework fuses them.

s9-011-ea16c5481c93a834.wav.text: And it comes with a free invariant.

s9-012-b9c433279e38fde1.wav.text: Every row of that gradient sums to exactly zero, because softmax sums to one and the one hot sums to one.
